headline: PSX extends the rally into Thu Aug 6 — KSE-100 up ~0.7% in early trade to ~181,335, adding to Wednesday's ~1.66% surge (close 180,015), on continued hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict; buying broad-based across autos, cement, banks, fertiliser, OMCs and power. Portfolio value ~Rs 9.96M, P/L +Rs 458K (+4.83%) on cost, up from +4.51% yesterday. Drawdown from the Jan ATH narrows further to ~4.3% (was 5.4%) — well short of the 10% deploy-dry-powder line. AVN's sell-half plan remains unexecuted — holdings still show the full 24,500 shares; this is the eighteenth straight review flagging it, with no fresh company news to explain the wait. EFERT's confirmed H1 2026 dividend ex-date (Rs 1.75/share) is Mon Aug 10 — 4 days out, enters the 3-day notification window tomorrow (Fri Aug 7). market: PSX extended its recovery into Thursday: the KSE-100 was up roughly 1,320 points (+0.73%) to around 181,335 in early trade, building on Wednesday's close of 180,014.93 (+2,931.71 points, +1.66%), as hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict continue to support sentiment — buying broad-based across automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, fertiliser, oil and gas exploration, OMCs and power generation. Against the Jan 23, 2026 all-time high of 189,556, the drawdown narrows to roughly 4.3% (from 5.4% yesterday) — well clear of the 10% line that would trigger deploying the AICF/MICF cash reserve; no change to the dry-powder plan. SBP's policy rate remains at 11.5% (held Jul 27, citing risks from renewed US-Iran hostilities); headline inflation eased to 11.1% in June; no new IMF program developments this week — stable macro backdrop. Mali's price feed (data/prices.json stamped 2026-08-06T09:28:39Z, ~14:28 PKT) shows modest broad-based gains consistent with the continued rally: CPHL Rs 76.25 (+2.1% day-over-day), NATF Rs 390.20 (+1.3%), MUGHAL Rs 82.79 (+1.0%), FFL Rs 16.60 (+1.2%), FABL Rs 100.30 (−2.0%, the only notable pullback), most others within ±1%; no holding moved more than ~2% so nothing crosses the >5% research-trigger threshold this review. Fund NAVs (ASSF, AKDISSF, NISIF, NISF, MIF, AICF, MICF, AKDISIF) are unchanged from yesterday's values since MUFAP publishes once daily near 21:30 PKT, after this review's data snapshot — consistent with the same daily-lag pattern noted the last several reviews, no action needed. On holdings: EFERT's Rs 1.75/share interim dividend ex-date is confirmed Aug 10, 2026 (payment Sep 3) — now 4 days out, enters the 3-day notify window tomorrow (Fri Aug 7); no news since the confirmed H1 results (profit -15.9% YoY consolidated, -34.6% YoY standalone) — checked again this review, nothing new. AVN: no fresh company news found this review either (checked board-meeting announcements again — still nothing since the Apr 30 FY25 final dividend declaration and May 23 AGM) — the position is exactly where it was, still the full 24,500 shares, with the stated "Monday Aug 3's open" execution window now three trading days gone. Either the trade happened off-app and index.html needs updating, or it's still pending — eighteen straight reviews is well past the point of this being a live decision rather than a stale one. AVN's Sep 2, 2026 earnings remains the outside deadline for a full exit if there's still no recovery — under four weeks away now. CPHL: no update since the Jul 8 REIT-demerger board approval — still a value-unlock story in motion, no urgency either way.

This confirms the glut thesis rather than reversing it: H1 urea sales hit a 10-year low at 537,000 tons, inventory swollen to 694,000 tons, discounts fully withdrawn Apr 4 (market share ~27%), new CEO Imran Ahmed (joined May 11) now delivering his first full set of weak numbers. The board still declared an interim dividend of Rs 1.75/share (17.5%) on top of the Rs 2.00/share (20%) already paid this year — yield is intact for now, ex-date confirmed Mon Aug 10, 2026 (payment Sep 3, now 4 days out, enters the 3-day notify window tomorrow). Keep for yield given the dividend held up, but this is now the second straight half with declining core earnings — rotate out if Q3/Q4 offtake doesn't recover or the next dividend gets cut outright.
